title: Graceful limiter failover and burst reconciliation across regions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We observed multiple incidents where the global quota/limiter service experienced transient outages or network partitions between regions, leading to two classes of customer-visible failures: (1) aggressive global throttling that persisted after primary recovered, and (2) uneven token reconciliation causing tenant unfairness (some customers lost burst credit while others retained it). Goal: design and implement a graceful limiter failover mode that preserves SLOs and tenant fairness during region-level failures and limiter node restarts. Scope: design limiter failover protocol, introduce write-ahead reconciliation (surge reconciliation window), circuit-breaker integration for downstream callers, and safe degradation rules (local permissive buffer with backpressure feedback). Not in scope: a full rewrite of quota model or billing changes.
acceptance_criteria: During simulated region partition tests, client request latency P95 increase <= 50ms for 90% of traffic when failing over to local permissive buffer
No tenant loses more than 5% of allocated burst tokens during a 5-minute limiter outage and subsequent reconciliation
Circuit-breaker metrics surface and automatically open when limiter coordination lag exceeds configured threshold
E2E canary deployment shows no increase in 5xx rate above 0.1% for affected routes during controlled failover
design_decisions: Use a two-tier model: local permissive token buffer (short-lived, conservative) + global authoritative quota store when available
Reconciliation strategy: operations log (compact WAL) + idempotent delta application with per-tenant watermark to avoid double-counting
Burst fairness: deterministic per-tenant reconciliation order based on consistent hashing and a rotating priority queue during backlog drain
Circuit breaker integration: limiter exposes coordination_lag_ms metric; downstream proxies use thresholded CB to switch from synchronous quota checks to permissive buffer mode
Backpressure signal: return HTTP 429 with X-Quota-Mode header and Retry-After; telemetry to track permissive buffer consumption
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime-1.20 rollout and canary in us-west-2 with 5% traffic
2) Run chaos monkey network partition tests for 10m windows against canary cluster
3) If metrics stable, increase to 25% then 100% over 72 hours with monitoring and abort criteria
4) Post-release: 7-day observation window and automated rollback if customer error budgets consumed
test_plan: Unit tests for WAL replay idempotency and watermark advancement
Integration tests: multi-region simulator that injects partition and enforces consistency invariants
Load test: synthetic tenants with skewed burst patterns to validate fairness algorithm under 50k rps
Chaos runbook: network partition, limiter process restart, and delayed WAL flush scenarios
SLO validation: synthetic clients exercising canary routes to measure P50/P95/P99 impact
comments: 2026-02-11 Marco Ruiz: Initial spike analysis attached. Root cause seems correlated with WAL compaction bug in limiter v1.19 (see incident-2026-02-09). Proposing permissive buffer fallback to avoid global hard-throttles.

2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Design review with PM and infra. PM requested stronger visibility for customers (header + dashboard). Action: add X-Quota-Mode header and a console chart for permissive buffer consumption.

2026-02-27 Devs: Implemented WAL delta format v2 and local buffer prototype. Local experiments show fairness drift under high tenant skew. Need deterministic reconciliation ordering; exploring rotating priority queue approach.
2026-03-03 Design review: UX approved X-Quota-Mode enum values ("permissive", "degraded", "authoritative"). Console telemetry event mapping agreed.

2026-03-08 SRE: Ran integration test with partition; observed P95 latency spike to 180ms for <1% traffic when buffer exhausted. Adjusted buffer sizing and failover thresholds. Update applied to branch feature/limiter-failover.
2026-03-12 QA: End-to-end canary started in us-west-2. Early metrics: 0.02% increase in 5xx (within tolerance). Continuing 24h soak. Preparing PR: github.com/redwood-inference/limiter/pull/312 (WIP).
